cohort: Pregnant women with overweight or obesity, randomized at 13-16 weeks' gestation to an exercise or non-exercising control group.
finding: Maternal exercise reduced the relative risk for cesarean birth in pregnant women, especially when controlling for race and BMI, and maternal exercise, pre-pregnancy fitness level, and gestational weight gain predicted neonatal birth weight.
mod_finding: Maternal exercise reduced the relative risk (RR) for cesarean birth from 1.63 to 1.43 when controlling for race and body mass index.
